verdict.rationale: Runpod documents Instant Clusters as fully managed multi-node compute where you can deploy jobs without managing infrastructure, networking, or cluster configuration. That covers the core of not building your own scheduling layer on raw nodes. However, no evidence names a managed Slurm or Kubernetes scheduler, so the specific scheduler the story asks for is unproven. Missing for 10: documented managed Slurm or Kubernetes support, job queueing/scheduling semantics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes

citations.quote: Instant Clusters provide fully managed multi-node compute with high-performance networking for distributed workloads. Deploy jobs or large-scale without managing infrastructure, networking, or cluster configuration.
Fully managed compute clusters for multi-node training and AI inference.
